title_en: Regulations on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en:
Article 5 The competent department of commerce, competent department of investment, and other relevant departments under the State Council shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, closely cooperate and collaborate with each other to jointly carry out the promotion, protection, and management of foreign investment.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the organization and leadership of the promotion, protection, and management of foreign investment, support and urge relevant departments to carry out the promotion, protection, and management of foreign investment in accordance with laws, regulations, and their respective functions and duties, and timely coordinate and resolve major issues in the promotion, protection, and management of foreign investment.

Article 6 The government and its relevant departments shall, in aspects such as government fund arrangements, land supply, tax and fee reductions, qualification licensing, standard setting, project application, and human resources policies, treat foreign-invested enterprises and domestic enterprises equally according to law.
Policies formulated by the government and its relevant departments to support enterprise development shall be made public according to law; for matters that require enterprises to apply for in the implementation of policies, the government and its relevant departments shall make public the conditions, procedures, time limits, etc. for application, and treat foreign-invested enterprises and domestic enterprises equally according to law during the review process.

Article 7 When formulating administrative regulations, rules, and normative documents related to foreign investment, or when the government and its relevant departments draft laws and local regulations related to foreign investment, they shall, based on the actual circumstances, adopt various forms such as soliciting written opinions and holding symposiums, feasibility studies meetings, and hearings to hear opinions and suggestions from foreign-invested enterprises and relevant chambers of commerce, associations, etc.; for opinions and suggestions that are concentrated or involve major rights and obligations of foreign-invested enterprises, the adoption of such opinions and suggestions shall be reported back through appropriate means.
Normative documents related to foreign investment shall be published in a timely manner according to law, and those not published shall not serve as the basis for administrative management. For normative documents closely related to the production and business operations of foreign-invested enterprises, the time between publication and implementation shall be reasonably determined based on actual circumstances.

Article 8 People's governments at all levels shall, in accordance with the principle of government-led and multi-party participation, establish and improve the foreign investment service system, and continuously improve the capabilities and standards of foreign investment services.

Article 9 The government and its relevant departments shall, through government websites and the national integrated online government service platform, concentrate on listing relevant laws, regulations, rules, normative documents, policies and measures, and investment project information related to foreign investment, and strengthen publicity and interpretation through various channels and methods, so as to provide foreign investors and foreign-invested enterprises with services such as consultation and guidance.

Article 10 'Special economic areas' as referred to in Article 13 of the Foreign Investment Law mean specific areas established with the approval of the state that implement more vigorous opening-up policies and measures.
Pilot policies and measures for foreign investment implemented by the state in certain regions, if proven feasible through practice, shall be promoted in other regions or nationwide based on actual circumstances.

Article 11 The state, based on the needs of national economic and social development, formulates a catalogue of industries encouraging foreign investment, specifying the particular industries, fields, and regions where foreign investors are encouraged and guided to invest. The catalogue of industries encouraging foreign investment shall be drafted by the competent department of investment under the State Council jointly with the competent department of commerce under the State Council and other relevant departments, and shall be submitted to the State Council for approval, and then published by the competent department of investment and the competent department of commerce under the State Council.

Article 12 Foreign investors and foreign-invested enterprises may, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, or provisions of the State Council, enjoy preferential treatment in terms of finance, taxation, finance, land use, etc.
If a foreign investor expands investment within China using its investment returns from within China, it shall enjoy corresponding preferential treatment according to law.

Article 13 Foreign-invested enterprises shall, according to law, participate equally with domestic enterprises in the formulation and revision of national standards, industry standards, local standards, and group standards. Foreign-invested enterprises may, as needed, formulate enterprise standards on their own or jointly with other enterprises.
Foreign-invested enterprises may submit proposals for setting up projects for standards to the competent administrative department for standardization and relevant competent administrative departments, put forward opinions and suggestions in the processes of standard project approval, drafting, technical review, and standard implementation information feedback, evaluation, etc., and undertake the relevant work of standard drafting, technical review, and foreign language translation of standards as provided.
The competent administrative department for standardization and relevant competent administrative departments shall establish and improve relevant working mechanisms, enhance the transparency of standard formulation and revision, and promote the disclosure of information in the entire process of standard formulation and revision.

Article 14 Mandatory standards formulated by the state shall apply equally to foreign-invested enterprises and domestic enterprises, and technical requirements higher than the mandatory standards shall not be applied specifically targeting foreign-invested enterprises.

Article 15 The government and its relevant departments shall not obstruct or restrict foreign-invested enterprises from freely entering the government procurement market in their regions and industries.
The procuring entities and procurement agencies of government procurement shall not apply differential treatment or discriminatory treatment to foreign-invested enterprises in terms of the publication of government procurement information, the determination of supplier conditions and qualification examination, bid evaluation criteria, etc., shall not limit suppliers based on forms of ownership, forms of organization, shareholding structure, nationality of investors, product or service brands, or other unreasonable conditions, and shall not treat differently the products produced or services provided by foreign-invested enterprises within China and those by domestic-funded enterprises.

Article 16 A foreign-invested enterprise may, in accordance with the Government Procurement Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Government Procurement Law) and its implementing regulations, raise inquiries or objections with the procuring entity or procurement agency, or file complaints with the government procurement supervision and administration department regarding matters of government procurement activities. The procuring entity, procurement agency, and government procurement supervision and administration department shall make a reply or a decision on handling within the prescribed time limit.

Article 17 The government procurement supervision and administration department and other relevant departments shall strengthen supervision and inspection of government procurement activities, and according to law, correct and investigate illegal or non-compliant acts such as applying differential treatment or discriminatory treatment to foreign-invested enterprises.

Article 18 A foreign-invested enterprise may, according to law, raise funds within or outside China by means of public issuance of stocks, corporate bonds, and other securities, as well as public or non-public issuance of other financing instruments, borrowing foreign debts, and other methods.

Article 19 A local people's government at or above the county level may, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, and local regulations, formulate policy measures for the promotion and facilitation of foreign investment in terms of fee reduction and exemption, land use quota guarantee, and provision of public services within its statutory authority.
When a local people's government at or above the county level formulates policy measures for the promotion and facilitation of foreign investment, it shall be oriented towards promoting high-quality development, be conducive to improving economic, social, and ecological benefits, and be conducive to continuously optimizing the foreign investment environment.

Article 20 The relevant competent departments shall compile and publish foreign investment guidelines to provide services and convenience for foreign investors and foreign-invested enterprises. The foreign investment guidelines shall include the introduction of the investment environment, the guide for foreign investment procedures, investment project information, and relevant data and information, and shall be updated in a timely manner.

Article 21 The State shall not expropriate the investments of foreign investors.
In special circumstances, where the State expropriates the investments of foreign investors for the needs of the public interest in accordance with legal provisions, it shall be conducted in accordance with statutory procedures and in a non-discriminatory manner, and compensation shall be given promptly based on the market value of the expropriated investment.
If a foreign investor is dissatisfied with the expropriation decision, it may apply for administrative reconsideration or file an administrative action according to law.

Article 22 The capital contributions, profits, capital gains, proceeds from asset disposal, royalties for intellectual property licenses obtained, compensation or damages received according to law, liquidation proceeds, and other amounts of foreign investors within China may be freely remitted in or out in RMB or foreign currency according to law. No unit or individual shall illegally restrict the currency, amount, frequency of remittance in or out, etc.
The wage income and other legitimate income of foreign employees and employees from Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan of foreign-invested enterprises may be freely remitted out according to law.

Article 23 The State shall increase the intensity of punishment for intellectual property infringement, continuously strengthen intellectual property enforcement, promote the establishment of a rapid collaborative protection mechanism for intellectual property, improve the diversified dispute resolution mechanism for intellectual property, and equally protect the intellectual property of foreign investors and foreign-invested enterprises.
Where patents of foreign investors or foreign-invested enterprises are involved in the formulation of standards, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant management provisions on standards involving patents.

Article 24 An administrative organ (including organizations authorized by laws and regulations to perform public affairs management functions, the same below) and its staff members shall not use the implementation of administrative licenses, administrative inspections, administrative penalties, administrative compulsion, or other administrative measures to force or indirectly force foreign investors or foreign-invested enterprises to transfer technology.

Article 25 Where an administrative authority, in performing its duties according to law, genuinely needs foreign investors or foreign-invested enterprises to provide materials or information involving trade secrets, it shall limit the request to the extent necessary for performing the duties, strictly control the scope of those who are privy to such materials or information, and personnel unrelated to the performance of the duties shall not have access to the relevant materials or information.
An administrative authority shall establish and improve internal management systems and take effective measures to protect the trade secrets of foreign investors and foreign-invested enterprises that it becomes aware of in the course of performing its duties; where it is necessary to share information with other administrative authorities according to law, it shall treat the trade secrets contained in the information confidentially to prevent disclosure.

Article 26 The government and its relevant departments, when formulating regulatory documents involving foreign investment, shall conduct legality review in accordance with the provisions of the State Council.
Where a foreign investor or foreign-invested enterprise considers that the regulatory document issued by a department of the State Council or by a local people's government or its department, which serves as the basis for an administrative act, is illegal, it may, when applying for administrative reconsideration or filing an administrative action against the administrative act according to law, simultaneously request a review of the regulatory document.

Article 27 The term "policy commitments" as used in Article 25 of the Foreign Investment Law refers to written commitments made by local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments, within their statutory authority, concerning the support policies, preferential treatment, and facilitations applicable to foreign investors and foreign-invested enterprises investing in their respective regions. The content of the policy commitments shall comply with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 28 Local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall fulfill the policy commitments made to foreign investors and foreign-invested enterprises according to law and the various contracts lawfully concluded, and shall not breach or repudiate contracts on grounds such as adjustment of administrative divisions, change of government, adjustment of institutions or functions, or replacement of responsible persons. Where it is necessary to change policy commitments or contractual provisions for the sake of national interest or public interest, such changes shall be made in accordance with the statutory authority and procedures, and the losses suffered by foreign investors or foreign-invested enterprises as a result shall be compensated in a timely, fair, and reasonable manner according to law.

Article 29 The people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall, in accordance with the principles of openness, transparency, efficiency, and convenience, establish and improve a complaint handling mechanism for foreign-invested enterprises, promptly address issues raised by foreign-invested enterprises or their investors, and coordinate to improve relevant policies and measures.
The competent commerce department of the State Council, together with the relevant departments of the State Council, shall establish an inter-ministerial joint conference system for complaints from foreign-invested enterprises, to coordinate and promote the handling of such complaints at the central level, and to guide and supervise the handling of such complaints at the local level. The local people's governments at or above the county level shall designate a department or institution responsible for receiving complaints from foreign-invested enterprises or their investors within their respective regions.
The competent commerce department of the State Council and the departments or institutions designated by local people's governments at or above the county level shall improve the working rules for complaint handling, diversify complaint channels, and specify the time limit for handling complaints. The working rules, complaint channels, and time limit for handling complaints shall be made public.

Article 30 Where a foreign-invested enterprise or its investor considers that an administrative act of an administrative authority or its personnel infringes upon its lawful rights and interests, and applies for coordination and resolution through the complaint handling mechanism for foreign-invested enterprises, the relevant party may, during the coordination, inquire about the situation of the administrative authority or its personnel against which the complaint is made, and the said administrative authority or its personnel shall cooperate. The result of the coordination shall be communicated in writing to the applicant in a timely manner.
Where a foreign-invested enterprise or its investor applies for coordination and resolution of the relevant issue in accordance with the preceding paragraph, it shall not affect its right to apply for administrative reconsideration or institute administrative proceedings according to law.

Article 31 No entity or individual shall suppress or retaliate against a foreign-invested enterprise or its investor for reporting issues or applying for coordination and resolution through the complaint handling mechanism for foreign-invested enterprises.
In addition to the complaint handling mechanism for foreign-invested enterprises, a foreign-invested enterprise or its investor may also report issues to the government and its relevant departments through other lawful channels.

Article 32 Foreign-invested enterprises may, according to law, establish chambers of commerce or associations. Unless otherwise provided by laws or regulations, a foreign-invested enterprise shall have the right to independently decide to join or withdraw from a chamber of commerce or association, and no entity or individual shall interfere.
Chambers of commerce and associations shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws, regulations, and their articles of association, strengthen industry self-discipline, promptly reflect industry demands, and provide services to their members in areas such as information consultation, publicity and training, market expansion, economic and trade exchanges, rights protection, and dispute resolution.
The State supports chambers of commerce and associations in conducting relevant activities in accordance with the provisions of laws, regulations, and their articles of association.

Article 33 Foreign investors shall not invest in fields where investment is prohibited under the negative list. Where fields where investment is restricted under the negative list are concerned, a foreign investor making an investment shall comply with the restrictive special access management measures specified in the negative list, such as equity requirements and senior officer requirements.

Article 34 Where, in the course of performing their duties according to law, the competent authorities find that a foreign investor intends to invest in a field covered by the negative list but does not meet the requirements of the negative list, they shall not process the relevant matters such as permits or enterprise registration; where the matter involves the approval of a fixed asset investment project, they shall not process the relevant approval matters.
The competent authorities shall strengthen supervision and inspection of the implementation of the provisions of the negative list. Where they discover that a foreign investor invests in a field where investment is prohibited under the negative list, or that the investment activities of a foreign investor violate the restrictive special access management measures stipulated in the negative list, they shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 36 of the Foreign Investment Law.

Article 35 Where a foreign investor invests in an industry or field that requires a license according to law, unless otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations, the relevant competent department responsible for implementing the license shall review the foreign investor's license application in accordance with conditions and procedures consistent with domestic investment, and shall not impose discriminatory requirements on foreign investors in terms of license conditions, application materials, review procedures, review time limits, etc.
The relevant competent department responsible for implementing the license shall optimize approval services and improve approval efficiency through various means. For license matters that meet relevant conditions and requirements, it may handle by means of notification and commitment in accordance with relevant provisions.
Article 36 Where foreign investment requires project approval or filing, it shall be handled in accordance with the relevant state provisions.

Article 37 The registration of foreign-invested enterprises shall be handled by the market supervision and administration department of the State Council or the market supervision and administration department of the local people's government authorized by it according to law. The market supervision and administration department of the State Council shall publish the list of authorized market supervision and administration departments.
The registered capital of a foreign-invested enterprise may be denominated in RMB or in a freely convertible currency.

Article 38 A foreign investor or foreign-invested enterprise shall submit investment information to the competent commerce department through the enterprise registration system and the enterprise credit information disclosure system. The competent commerce department and the market supervision and administration department of the State Council shall ensure the interfacing and coordination of relevant business systems, and provide guidance for foreign investors or foreign-invested enterprises in submitting investment information.

Article 39 The content, scope, frequency, and specific procedures of the foreign investment information report shall be determined and published by the competent commerce department of the State Council in conjunction with the market supervision and administration department of the State Council and other relevant departments in accordance with the principles of necessity, efficiency, and convenience. The competent commerce department and other relevant departments shall strengthen information sharing; investment information that can be obtained through inter-departmental information sharing shall not be required to be submitted again by foreign investors or foreign-invested enterprises.
The investment information submitted by a foreign investor or foreign-invested enterprise shall be true, accurate, and complete.
Article 40 The State shall establish a security review system for foreign investment, conducting security reviews of foreign investment that affects or may affect national security.

Article 42 Where a procurer or procurement agency in government procurement imposes differential treatment or discriminatory treatment on foreign-invested enterprises under unreasonable conditions, it shall be held legally liable in accordance with the Government Procurement Law and its implementing regulations; if it affects or may affect the results of winning the bid or concluding the transaction, it shall be handled in accordance with the Government Procurement Law and its implementing regulations.
Where the supervisory department for government procurement fails to handle a complaint from a foreign-invested enterprise within the time limit, the person directly in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 43 Where an administrative organ or its staff member uses administrative means to compel or covertly compel a foreign investor or foreign-invested enterprise to transfer technology, the person directly in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 44 Foreign-invested enterprises established prior to the coming into force of the Foreign Investment Law in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-foreign Equity Joint Ventures, the Law of the People's Republic of China on Wholly Foreign-owned Enterprises, and the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-foreign Contractual Joint Ventures (hereinafter referred to as existing foreign-invested enterprises) may, within five years after the coming into force of the Foreign Investment Law, adjust their organizational form, organizational structure, etc. in accordance with the provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China, and other laws, and undergo modification registration according to law, or may continue to retain their original organizational form, organizational structure, etc.
From January 1, 2025, for existing foreign-invested enterprises that have not adjusted their organizational form, organizational structure, etc. and undergone modification registration according to law, the market supervision and administration department shall not handle other registration matters applied for by them, and shall publicize the relevant circumstances.

Article 45 The specific matters concerning the change registration of the organizational form and organizational structure of existing foreign-invested enterprises shall be prescribed and published by the market supervision and administration department of the State Council. The market supervision and administration department of the State Council shall strengthen guidance on change registration, and the market supervision and administration department responsible for handling change registration shall optimize services through multiple means to facilitate enterprises in handling change registration.

Article 46 After the organizational form, organizational structure, etc. of an existing foreign-invested enterprise are adjusted according to law, the methods for transfer of equity or rights and interests, distribution of profits, and distribution of residual properties as agreed in the contract between the original joint venture or cooperative parties may continue to be handled in accordance with the agreement.
Article 47 Where a foreign-invested enterprise invests within the territory of China, the relevant provisions of the Foreign Investment Law and these Regulations shall apply.

Article 48 Investors from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Macao Special Administrative Region who invest in the mainland shall be handled by reference to the Foreign Investment Law and these Regulations; if laws, administrative regulations, or the State Council provide otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.
Investors from the Taiwan region who invest in the mainland shall be governed by the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Investments by Compatriots from Taiwan (hereinafter referred to as the Law on Protection of Investments by Compatriots from Taiwan) and its implementing rules; matters not provided for in the Law on Protection of Investments by Compatriots from Taiwan and its implementing rules shall be handled by reference to the Foreign Investment Law and these Regulations.
Chinese citizens residing abroad who invest within the territory of China shall be handled by reference to the Foreign Investment Law and these Regulations; if laws, administrative regulations, or the State Council provide otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 49 These Regulations shall come into force on January 1, 2020. The Implementing Regulations of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures, the Interim Provisions on the Term of Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures, the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprises, and the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Contractual Joint Ventures shall be abolished simultaneously.
If any provisions concerning foreign investment formulated before January 1, 2020 are inconsistent with the Foreign Investment Law and these Regulations, the provisions of the Foreign Investment Law and these Regulations shall prevail.
